sentences.text: 1 This application under section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 has been filed by the petitioners, namely, (1) Barnali Das and (2) Saru Das @ Charu Bala Das, who are detained behind the bars since 13.10.2023 in connection with Hajo P.S. Case No. 614/2023 under Section 120B/498A/302 of the Indian Penal Code.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-4 vs The State Of Assam on 17 November, 2023.json

sentences.text:
The gist of accusation against the present petitioners is that on 12.10.2023, one Mitu Das has lodged an FIR before the Officer-In-Charge of Hajo Police Station, inter-alia, alleging that the sister of the first informant, namely, Manisha Das eloped with the accused No. 1 named in the FIR, namely,
Deepjyoti Das and were living a marital life thereafter.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-4 vs The State Of Assam on 17 November, 2023.json

sentences.text: However, it is alleged in the FIR that after that she was subjected to physical and mental torture.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-4 vs The State Of Assam on 17 November, 2023.json

sentences.text: It is further alleged in the FIR that on 12.10.2023, the accused persons named in the FIR had killed the sister of the first informant and have tried to give it a colour of suicide.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-4 vs The State Of Assam on 17 November, 2023.json

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the petitioners has submitted that both the petitioners are woman and petitioner No. 1 is the sister-in-law and petitioner No. 2 is the mother-in-law of the deceased.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-4 vs The State Of Assam on 17 November, 2023.json

sentences.text: It is further submitted that the allegations levelled against the present petitoner is not true.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-4 vs The State Of Assam on 17 November, 2023.json

sentences.text:
It is also submitted by the learned counsel for the petitioners that in the Page No.# 3/4 meanwhile,
the husband of the deceased, namely, Deepjyoti Das has already been arrested.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-4 vs The State Of Assam on 17 November, 2023.json

sentences.text:
It is also submitted that there was some matrimonial dispute between the husband and wife due to which the deceased has committed suicide and the petitioners are no way involved in the death of the Manisha Das.
On the other hand, learned Additional Public Prosecutor has vehemently opposed the grant of bail to the present petitioners on the ground that though the post-mortem examination report is available in the case diary, however, it is found in the post-mortem report that no opinion has yet been given by the doctors, who conducted the post-mortem examination report.
It is also submitted by the learned Additional Public Prosecutor that it is suspected that the deceased might have been administered some poison and which may be ascertained only after receipt of the FSL report.
I have considered the submissions made by learned counsel for both the sides and has perused the materials available in the case diary including the post-mortem examination report of the deceased.
It appears that though the final opinion as regard to cause of death has been kept pending till the receipt of the chemical and toxicological examination report, however, at this stage, it appears that the ligature marks were found on the neck of the deceased and she was found hanging when her dead body was recovered.
It further appears from the case diary that Investigating Officer has recorded the statement of witnesses who are neighbours of the present petitioners and they have stated before the Page No.# 1/4 vs The State Of Assam on 17 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/44107029/
2 Investigating Officer that their used to be occasional quarrels between the family members of the petitioners as well as the deceased.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-4 vs The State Of Assam on 17 November, 2023.json

sentences.text: Nothing apart from this is available in the case diary at this stage and Page No.# 4/4 therefore, it appears that at this stage apart from suspicion there is nothing else against the present petitioners to justify their further detention for the sake of fair investigation of this case, if they otherwise co-operates in the investigation.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-4 vs The State Of Assam on 17 November, 2023.json

sentences.text: It also appears that the submissions made by learned Additional Public Prosecutor that the petitioners might have been administered poison does not find any support from any of the witnesses whose statement has been recorded by the Investigating Officer.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-4 vs The State Of Assam on 17 November, 2023.json

sentences.text:
In view of above, the above-named petitioners, are hereby allowed to go on bail of Rs. 30,000/- each with a suitable surety of like amount to the satisfaction of the learned Judicial Magistrate First Class, Hajo, Kamrup with following conditions that:-
(i) both the above-named petitioners shall co-operate in the investigation and shall appear before the Investigating Officer as and when so required for the sake of fair completion of the investigation of the case; and (ii) both the above-named petitioners shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement threat or promise to the victim or to any other persons who may be acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade such person from disclosing such facts before the Investigating Officer or to any Court.
With the above observations, this bail application is hereby disposed of.

4) On 08.02.2018, the petitioner No.2 i.e., Musst. Sufia Begum had lodged an FIR before the Officer In-Charge of Dispur Police Station, inter-alia, alleging that her husband Amdadul Hazarika, who is the petitioner No.1 in this case used to torture her after consuming "Bhang" and on 07.02.2018 he throw the petitioner No.2 out of his house and also tried to assault her with a Dao.

5) The learned counsel for the petitioners has submitted that both the petitioners are husband and wife in relationship and they have two grown up college going children,

sentences.text: It is also submitted by the learned Senior Counsel for the petitioners that the petitioners have amicably settled their dispute amongst themselves and are now residing peacefully in a rented house with their children.

sentences.text: The learned Senior Counsel for the petitioners have also submitted that considering the settlement, which has been raised between the parties, there is a weak chance of conviction in the case and, therefore, proceeding with the PRC Case No.1850/2021 would only be an abuse of the process of Court.

sentences.text:
7) The learned counsel for the petitioners have also cited the following rulings in support of his submissions:

 ii. Badana Begum (Musstt) v. State of Assam  reported in 2013 1 GLT 692.
8) I have considered the submissions made by the learned counsel for both the sides and I have perused the material available on record, this application has been jointly filed by both the petitioners, who are husband and wife in relationship, which itself shows that they have amicably settled their dispute amongst themselves.

sentences.text: Though the Section 498A of the Indian Penal Code under which the Charge-sheet has been laid which is a non compoundable offence, however, there are catena of rulings of the Apex Court as well as of this Court that in dispute between the family members more so, in matrimonial dispute, where the parties have reached amicable settlement amongst themselves and where there is a bleak chance of conviction in the pending trial, it would be a futile exercise to proceed with the pending trial and proceeding with such a trial may amount to abuse of the process of Court.

sentences.text: 10) It also appears from the Charge-sheet that the petitioner No.2 is listed in the Charge-sheet as the main witness for the prosecution side and when she has herself settled the dispute with her husband, hence there is unlikelihood Page No.# 4/4 that the pending Criminal Case against the petitioner No.1 will result in conviction.

sentences.text: 11) Under such circumstances, this Court is of the considered opinion that this is a fit case where the Charge-sheet and the pending case against the petitioner No.1 may be quashed by invoking powers of this Court under Section 528 of the BNSS.

sentences.text: 12) Accordingly, the Charge-sheet filed in PRC Case No.1850/2021 against the petitioner No.1 is hereby quashed.

This application under Section 482 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 has been filed by the petitioner, namely, Jahangir Alom, who is apprehending his arrest in connection with Dhubri P.S. Case No. 314/2022, under Sections 379/411 of IPC, 1860 read with Section 13 of the Assam Cattle Preservation Act, 2021 corresponding to PRC Case No. 62/2024.
3.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-4 vs The State Of Assam on 3 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: The learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that in the aforesaid case, charge sheet has already been laid.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-4 vs The State Of Assam on 3 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: However, the petitioner apprehends that as one of the offence under which charge sheet has been laid under Section 13(1) of the Assam Cattle Preservation Act, 2021, which is exclusively triable by the Court of the learned Sessions.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-4 vs The State Of Assam on 3 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: Hence, the Court of the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate may not grant bail to the petitioner in the light of the observations made by the Apex Court in the case of "Prahlad Singh Bhati Vs. N.C.T., Delhi & Anr." reported in "(2021) 4 SCC 280," wherein the Apex Court has observed that even though there is no legal bar for the Magistrate to consider an application for grant of bail to a person who is arrested for an offence exclusively triable by the Court of Sessions yet it would be proper and appropriate that in such case the Magistrate directs the accused person to approach the Court of Sessions for the purpose of getting the relief of bail.

entities.text: Prahlad Singh Bhati Vs. N.C.T., Delhi & Anr." reported in "(2021) 4 SCC 280
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-4 vs The State Of Assam on 3 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: 4. I have considered the submissions of the learned counsel for both sides and perused the case record.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-4 vs The State Of Assam on 3 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: 5. The observations of the Apex Court in the above referred case of Prahlad Singh (supra) was made in a case which involved offence under Page No.# 3/4 Sections 302/406/498A of IPC, therefore, the same has to be applied only in cases of those nature in context of which the said observations was made.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-4 vs The State Of Assam on 3 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: It is also important to note that in an offence under Section 302 of IPC, there was also an embargo under Section 437(1)(i) of the Cr.P.C., 1973 in granting bail in offences which entails punishment of life imprisonment or death penalty.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-4 vs The State Of Assam on 3 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: The observations made by the Apex Court in the case of Prahlad Singh (supra) should not be read out of context in which it was made.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-4 vs The State Of Assam on 3 September, 2025.json

sentences.text:
6. However, in the instant case, the offence involved is under Section 13(1) of Assam Cattle Preservation Act, 2021, which, though, an offence exclusively triable by the Court of Sessions,
however, the maximum punishment prescribed for the said offence is 8 (Eight) years only and no embargo is there on the Court of learned Sub-Divisional Judicial Magistrate, Dhubri to consider an application for granting bail if it thinks fit to do so under the facts and circumstances of a particular case.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-4 vs The State Of Assam on 3 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: 7. This Court is, therefore, of the considered opinion that the apprehension that the Court of learned Sub-Divisional Judicial Magistrate, Dhubri, may not grant bail to the petitioner after he appears before the said Court in pursuant to the notices received by him, does not have any legal basis.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-4 vs The State Of Assam on 3 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: 8. This Anticipatory Bail application is accordingly disposed of with an observation that the petitioner may appear before the Trial Court on the next date fixed i.e. 09.10.2025 and may pray for regular bail before the said Court, if so advised.

opennyai_summary.17_November_2023__facts:
The gist of accusation against the present petitioners is that on 12.10.2023, one Mitu Das has lodged an FIR before the Officer-In-Charge of Hajo Police Station, inter-alia, alleging that the sister of the first informant, namely, Manisha Das eloped with the accused No. 1 named in the FIR, namely,
Deepjyoti Das and were living a marital life thereafter.
However, it is alleged in the FIR that after that she was subjected to physical and mental torture.
It is further alleged in the FIR that on 12.10.2023, the accused persons named in the FIR had killed the sister of the first informant and have tried to give it a colour of suicide.
opennyai_summary.17_November_2023__arguments:
It is also submitted that there was some matrimonial dispute between the husband and wife due to which the deceased has committed suicide and the petitioners are no way involved in the death of the Manisha Das.
On the other hand, learned Additional Public Prosecutor has vehemently opposed the grant of bail to the present petitioners on the ground that though the post-mortem examination report is available in the case diary, however, it is found in the post-mortem report that no opinion has yet been given by the doctors, who conducted the post-mortem examination report.
It is also submitted by the learned Additional Public Prosecutor that it is suspected that the deceased might have been administered some poison and which may be ascertained only after receipt of the FSL report.
I have considered the submissions made by learned counsel for both the sides and has perused the materials available in the case diary including the post-mortem examination report of the deceased.
It appears that though the final opinion as regard to cause of death has been kept pending till the receipt of the chemical and toxicological examination report, however, at this stage, it appears that the ligature marks were found on the neck of the deceased and she was found hanging when her dead body was recovered.
It further appears from the case diary that Investigating Officer has recorded the statement of witnesses who are neighbours of the present petitioners and they have stated before the Page No.# 1/4 vs The State Of Assam on 17 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/44107029/
2 Investigating Officer that their used to be occasional quarrels between the family members of the petitioners as well as the deceased.
opennyai_summary.17_November_2023__decision:
In view of above, the above-named petitioners, are hereby allowed to go on bail of Rs. 30,000/- each with a suitable surety of like amount to the satisfaction of the learned Judicial Magistrate First Class, Hajo, Kamrup with following conditions that:-
(i) both the above-named petitioners shall co-operate in the investigation and shall appear before the Investigating Officer as and when so required for the sake of fair completion of the investigation of the case; and (ii) both the above-named petitioners shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement threat or promise to the victim or to any other persons who may be acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade such person from disclosing such facts before the Investigating Officer or to any Court.
With the above observations, this bail application is hereby disposed of.

opennyai_summary.10_September_2024__facts:
2) This application under Section 528 of the BNSS, 2023 has been jointly filed by the petitioners,
namely, Shri. Amdadul Hazarika and Musst. Sufia Begum praying for quashing of the Charge-sheet and the PRC case number which arose out of the said Charge-sheet PRC Case No.1850/2021 pending in the Court of learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Kamrup (Metro).
3) The facts relevant for consideration of the instant Criminal Petition, in brief, are as follows:
4) On 08.02.2018, the petitioner No.2 i.e., Musst. Sufia Begum had lodged an FIR before the Officer In-Charge of Dispur Police Station, inter-alia, alleging that her husband Amdadul Hazarika, who is the petitioner No.1 in this case used to torture her after consuming "Bhang" and on 07.02.2018 he throw the petitioner No.2 out of his house and also tried to assault her with a Dao.
opennyai_summary.10_September_2024__arguments:
The learned Senior Counsel for the petitioners have also submitted that considering the settlement, which has been raised between the parties, there is a weak chance of conviction in the case and, therefore, proceeding with the PRC Case No.1850/2021 would only be an abuse of the process of Court.
7) The learned counsel for the petitioners have also cited the following rulings in support of his submissions:
i. Jasmair Singh and Another v. State of  Haryana and Another reported in 2022 9SCC 73.
 ii. Badana Begum (Musstt) v. State of Assam  reported in 2013 1 GLT 692.
8) I have considered the submissions made by the learned counsel for both the sides and I have perused the material available on record, this application has been jointly filed by both the petitioners, who are husband and wife in relationship, which itself shows that they have amicably settled their dispute amongst themselves.
opennyai_summary.10_September_2024__ANALYSIS:
Though the Section 498A of the Indian Penal Code under which the Charge-sheet has been laid which is a non compoundable offence, however, there are catena of rulings of the Apex Court as well as of this Court that in dispute between the family members more so, in matrimonial dispute, where the parties have reached amicable settlement amongst themselves and where there is a bleak chance of conviction in the pending trial, it would be a futile exercise to proceed with the pending trial and proceeding with such a trial may amount to abuse of the process of Court.
10) It also appears from the Charge-sheet that the petitioner No.2 is listed in the Charge-sheet as the main witness for the prosecution side and when she has herself settled the dispute with her husband, hence there is unlikelihood Page No.# 4/4 that the pending Criminal Case against the petitioner No.1 will result in conviction.
11) Under such circumstances, this Court is of the considered opinion that this is a fit case where the Charge-sheet and the pending case against the petitioner No.1 may be quashed by invoking powers of this Court under Section 528 of the BNSS.
opennyai_summary.10_September_2024__decision:
12) Accordingly, the Charge-sheet filed in PRC Case No.1850/2021 against the petitioner No.1 is hereby quashed.
13) This Criminal Petition accordingly disposed of.

opennyai_summary.final__arguments:
The learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that in the aforesaid case, charge sheet has already been laid.
However, the petitioner apprehends that as one of the offence under which charge sheet has been laid under Section 13(1) of the Assam Cattle Preservation Act, 2021, which is exclusively triable by the Court of the learned Sessions.
opennyai_summary.final__ANALYSIS:
Hence, the Court of the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate may not grant bail to the petitioner in the light of the observations made by the Apex Court in the case of "Prahlad Singh Bhati Vs. N.C.T., Delhi & Anr." reported in "(2021) 4 SCC 280," wherein the Apex Court has observed that even though there is no legal bar for the Magistrate to consider an application for grant of bail to a person who is arrested for an offence exclusively triable by the Court of Sessions yet it would be proper and appropriate that in such case the Magistrate directs the accused person to approach the Court of Sessions for the purpose of getting the relief of bail.
The observations made by the Apex Court in the case of Prahlad Singh (supra) should not be read out of context in which it was made.
6. However, in the instant case, the offence involved is under Section 13(1) of Assam Cattle Preservation Act, 2021, which, though, an offence exclusively triable by the Court of Sessions,
however, the maximum punishment prescribed for the said offence is 8 (Eight) years only and no embargo is there on the Court of learned Sub-Divisional Judicial Magistrate, Dhubri to consider an application for granting bail if it thinks fit to do so under the facts and circumstances of a particular case.
